newsitem.title: INDIA: India soymeal prices rise on firm export demand.
newsitem.headline: India soymeal prices rise on firm export demand.

text.p: Good export demand and poor arrivals firmed Indian soymeal prices by $5-6 per tonne in the past week, traders said on Tuesday.
They said exporters were waiting for a further rise in prices before signing new contracts.
"Reports of good export demand pushed up prices," said one oilmeal broker. "Exporters are offering limited quantities on hopes of getting better prices later."
Traders said soymeal was currently quoted at $295-296 per tonne FAS compared with $290 a week ago.
Indian exporters have so far signed contracts for 1.9 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (November-October) season, traders said.
Domestic soybean arrivals were about 2,000 tonnes per day compared with nearly 15,000 tonnes same time a year ago in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean industry.
Soybean was quoted at 11,600-12,000 rupees per tonne against 9,700-10,000 rupees at the same time last year.
Traders said farmers were holding back stocks on hopes of getting better prices in the future.
"Farmers are creating stocks to get higher prices," said Manoharlal Jain, a soymeal broker.
Traders said capacity utilisation was around 15 percent compared with 80-90 percent at the same time last year. --New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
